title: BillBook
tagline: Billing app for small shop owners in Gujarat
pitch: You are building a simple billing and credit tracking app for small shop owners in Gujarat. It's software that businesses pay for every month. You have ₹2 crore from angel investors. In about two years you must reach 50,000 shops using it every month, earn as much as you spend each month, and keep owners' trust.

stages.title: Find the real problem
stages.situation: You want to build software that helps small shop owners run their business. You have one month to learn what they struggle with.

options.label: Email a survey to 5,000 shops from a business list
options.outcome: Few replies, mostly from bigger shops with an accountant. They ask for 'reports'.
options.lesson: Small shop owners rarely read email. The survey heard from the wrong users.

later.note: Shops who joined for 'reports' never opened them. The real daily pain was elsewhere.

options.label: Sit behind the counter at 25 shops in Surat for 3 weeks
options.outcome: The real pain: writing bills by hand, and chasing customers who owe money (udhaar). Owners lose thousands a month to forgotten dues.
options.lesson: Watching real work shows the costly problem the owner never thinks to mention.

options.label: Copy the features of big accounting software
options.outcome: You build for accountants. Shop owners find it confusing.
options.lesson: Copying a product built for different users gives you their features, not your users' needs.

stages.title: Pick your first users
stages.situation: Who do you build for first?

options.label: Kirana and medical shops in Gujarat, run by the owner
options.detail: One type of shop, daily billing, lots of udhaar.
options.outcome: Owners in the same market talk to each other every day.
options.lesson: A narrow first user lets you build something they love, and they spread it.

options.label: Every kind of business in India
options.outcome: Restaurants, factories and shops need different things. You build a little for each.
options.lesson: Serving everyone at once makes you average for everyone.

options.label: Big wholesalers with 50 staff
options.outcome: They want custom features and long sales cycles.
options.lesson: Big customers bring money and demands that pull you away from your product.

later.note: Two big wholesalers left for enterprise software, and their partner shops went with them.

stages.title: Build the first version
stages.situation: You have two months to launch.

options.label: Bills on the phone in Gujarati, plus automatic WhatsApp reminders for udhaar
options.outcome: Owners collect old dues in the first week. They are amazed.
options.lesson: An MVP that delivers money back in week one sells itself.

options.label: A full system: stock, staff, GST, accounts, reports
options.outcome: Owners open it once, get lost, and go back to paper.
options.lesson: Too many features scare new users. Start with the one job they care about.

options.label: Store all data only on the phone, no backup
options.outcome: Works fine until a phone is lost.
options.lesson: For a business, losing records is a disaster. Reliability is part of the product.

later.note: Dozens of shops lost their phones and every record with them. Angry videos are spreading.

stages.title: Set the price
stages.situation: Shop owners are careful with money. How do you charge?

options.label: Free for basic bills, ₹99 a month for udhaar reminders and GST
options.outcome: Most start free. Many pay once reminders bring back money.
options.lesson: Charge for the feature that clearly makes users money. The price feels small next to the gain.

options.label: Free forever, earn from ads later
options.outcome: Shops join fast. Server and support costs pile up.
options.lesson: Free with no plan trains users that your product is worth nothing.

later.note: You started charging. Many shops went back to paper the same week.

options.label: ₹4,999 a year, paid upfront
options.outcome: Few small shops can pay that much at once.
options.lesson: Price and payment style must fit how your users handle money.

stages.title: Launch
stages.situation: How do you get your first big wave of shops?

options.label: Visit markets with local agents who set it up on the shop owner's phone
options.outcome: Owners see it working in 5 minutes and tell the shop next door.
options.lesson: For users new to software, a helping hand at the start is the best channel.

options.label: ₹30 lakh on Facebook and YouTube ads
options.outcome: Installs jump. Many owners can't set it up alone.
options.lesson: Installs that never finish setup are wasted money.

later.note: Most shops from the ads got stuck on the first screen and gave up.

options.label: Referral: a free month for both shops
options.outcome: Whole markets join together.
options.lesson: Referrals bring users like your best users.

stages.title: First week experience
stages.situation: Many shops make 2 bills and stop. What do you fix?

options.label: Help them add their top 50 items and send their first udhaar reminder on day one
options.outcome: Shops see money come back in days and keep using it.
options.lesson: Activation means reaching the first real value fast.

options.label: Send 3 'Grow your business!' messages a day
options.outcome: Owners find it annoying and block you.
options.lesson: Messages can't replace value.

options.label: ₹50 cashback for every 10 bills
options.outcome: Some make fake bills for cashback.
options.lesson: Rewards can be gamed. Reward real value.

stages.title: Choose your north star
stages.situation: The team needs one number to chase every week.

options.label: Shops that make bills on at least 20 days a month
options.outcome: The team works on speed, reminders and help.
options.lesson: A good north star shows the product has become part of the user's day.

options.label: App downloads
options.outcome: Marketing wins, the product suffers.
options.lesson: Downloads don't show value.

options.label: Total value of bills made
options.outcome: A few big shops make the number look great while small shops quit.
options.lesson: A total can hide what most users experience.

stages.title: Grow the team
stages.situation: You have 15,000 shops. Who do you hire?

options.label: A customer success lead and a support team who speak Gujarati and Hindi
options.outcome: Problems are solved in minutes. Shops renew.
options.lesson: For business software, support is part of the product.

options.label: 15 sales agents paid only on sign ups
options.outcome: Sign ups jump. Many agents make false promises.
options.lesson: Paying only for sign ups rewards the wrong behaviour.

later.note: Shops found the app couldn't do what agents promised. Refund requests are piling up.

options.label: Stay lean, founders do support
options.outcome: You save money but the founders are exhausted.
options.lesson: Burnout is a real cost.

later.note: Support calls went unanswered for days during GST filing week.

stages.title: Raise money
stages.situation: Investors are interested. How much do you raise?

options.label: ₹10 crore, promise 10 lakh shops in a year
options.outcome: Huge cash, huge expectations.
options.lesson: Growing before the product is ready copies your problems everywhere.

later.note: To keep your promise, you hired 200 agents across India. Costs exploded, quality fell.

options.label: ₹3 crore from founders of business software companies
options.outcome: Enough runway, and investors who know how to sell software to small businesses.
options.lesson: Smart money brings advice, not just cash.

options.label: Don't raise. Aim for profit.
options.outcome: You stay careful, but growth slows.
options.lesson: Not raising is valid, with a clear path to profit.

stages.title: Build a growth engine
stages.situation: You want growth that keeps going on its own. What do you build?

options.label: Every WhatsApp bill and reminder says 'Made with BillBook', with a link
options.outcome: Customers and suppliers who get bills ask about it. Many are shop owners too.
options.lesson: When using the product shows it to others, growth runs by itself. That's a viral loop.

options.label: TV ads on business news
options.outcome: A spike, mostly from people who never set it up.
options.lesson: Expensive spikes don't build lasting growth.

later.note: Most TV sign ups never made a second bill.

options.label: Add versions for restaurants and salons
options.outcome: Users grow, but each new type of shop needs its own features.
options.lesson: New markets bring growth and new costs.

stages.title: Earn more per shop
stages.situation: You need more money per shop. What do you try?

options.label: Show supplier ads inside the app
options.outcome: Some income. Some owners find it cluttered.
options.lesson: Ads can work if they don't get in the way.

options.label: Double the monthly price
options.outcome: Revenue jumps, many shops cancel.
options.lesson: Price rises must match the value users see.

options.label: Small business loans based on billing history, with a bank partner
options.outcome: Slow start. Repayments are good because you know these shops.
options.lesson: Your product data can unlock a valuable service, if used carefully and with permission.

later.note: Shops repay on time. Your loan commission is now a big income line.

stages.title: A giant enters
stages.situation: A big payments company launches free billing software for shops.

options.label: Make everything free too
options.outcome: Shops stay, but you are burning cash fast.
options.lesson: Price wars favour the player with the most money.

later.note: The free war ended. Your cash is gone, and price hunters moved on.

options.label: Ignore price. Double down on udhaar collection and local support
options.outcome: Some shops try the free app. It has no local support.
options.lesson: Compete on your strengths.

later.note: Shops came back. 'Free is useless if nobody picks up the phone,' one owner said.

options.label: Pivot to selling to big companies
options.outcome: Small shops feel dropped. The team is confused.
options.lesson: Running from competition throws away what you built.

stages.title: A crisis
stages.situation: A bug sent udhaar reminders with wrong amounts to thousands of customers. Shop owners are embarrassed.

options.label: Apologise to every shop, send corrections, give a free month
options.outcome: It costs money, but owners respect the honesty.
options.lesson: Handling a mistake openly can build more trust.

options.label: Say nothing and hope it's forgotten
options.outcome: Owners find out from their customers. They're furious.
options.lesson: Hiding a mistake makes it much worse.

options.label: Blame the WhatsApp service
options.outcome: Owners don't believe it. Your engineers are upset.
options.lesson: Users hold you responsible for your whole product.

stages.title: Your local agents want a better deal
stages.situation: The local agents who set up shops say their pay is too low. Some work for rivals now.

options.label: Raise pay and give them a share of renewals
options.outcome: Costs rise, but agents care about shops staying, not just signing up.
options.lesson: Pay partners for the long-term result you want.

options.label: Stop using agents, move to online sign up only
options.outcome: New shops get stuck without help.
options.lesson: Removing the help your users rely on costs more than it saves.

options.label: Pay agents only for shops that stay 3 months
options.outcome: Good agents earn more. Some new ones quit.
options.lesson: Paying for outcomes can work, if it's fair.

stages.title: The road to profit
stages.situation: Investors want a clear path to profit before the next round.

options.label: Stop the 3 business types that rarely pay
options.outcome: Some shops leave, but costs fall a lot.
options.lesson: Cutting losing parts focuses the business on what works.

options.label: Launch in 10 new states now
options.outcome: Big new costs before the core is profitable.
options.lesson: Expanding to escape problems usually multiplies them.

options.label: Raise prices 5%
options.outcome: A bit more revenue. Some shops leave.
options.lesson: Small price changes add up, but watch trust and growth.

events.title: GST rules change overnight
events.situation: A new GST rule starts next week. Shops are confused.

options.label: Update the app in 3 days and send simple Gujarati guides
options.outcome: Shops rush to you for help.
options.lesson: Helping users through a change wins them for years.

options.label: Update it next month
options.outcome: Shops file wrong bills and blame you.
options.lesson: Being late when users need you most hurts trust.

events.title: Your servers go down
events.situation: On a Saturday evening, the app stops syncing bills.

options.label: Let the app work offline and tell shops right away
options.outcome: Shops keep billing. Data syncs later.
options.lesson: Have a backup plan for your users' busiest moments.

options.label: Fix it quietly
options.outcome: Owners panic that bills are lost.
options.lesson: Silence in a crisis feels like not caring.

events.title: A rival poaches your tech lead
events.situation: Your tech lead has an offer at double the pay.

options.label: Counter-offer with equity
options.outcome: They stay.
options.lesson: Key people are worth investing in.

options.label: Let them go and promote from within
options.outcome: A few bugs slip through during the handover.
options.lesson: Losing key people has a cost.

events.title: Diwali rush
events.situation: Shops are busier than ever. Billing volume triples.

options.label: Add capacity early and keep support open late
options.outcome: Everything works. Shops tell other shops.
options.lesson: Prepare for known peaks.

options.label: Run as normal
options.outcome: The app slows at the busiest hour.
options.lesson: Failing at the peak hurts trust the most.
